if [ "$v" -gt 0 ] && [ "$v" -le 900 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/UserVars/HostClientSessionTimeout = $v (expected 1-900)"; fi

remediation.guidance: 1. Set the approved idle timeout with Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name UserVars.HostClientSessionTimeout | Set-AdvancedSetting -Value <seconds> -Confirm:$false 2. Reconnect to the Host Client and confirm inactive sessions expire as expected.

title: Host must have an accurate DCUI.Access list
description: The DCUI.Access parameter in VMware ESXi is used to specify a list of users who are permitted to access the Direct Console User Interface (DCUI) of the ESXi host, especially when Lockdown Mode is enabled. This parameter helps in controlling and securing access to the ESXi host by allowing only authorized users to override Lockdown Mode and access the DCUI, particularly in ... Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 3.18 Host must have an accurate DCUI.Access list

audit.command: To verify a proper trusted users list is set for DCUI, perform the following from the vSphere web client: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand System. 3. Select Advanced System Settings then click Edit. 4. Enter DCUI.Access in the filter. 5. Verify that the DCUI.Access attribute is set to a comma-separated list of the users who are allowed to override lockdown mode. Alternately, the following PowerCLI command may be used: Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name DCUI.Access

remediation.command: To set a trusted users list for DCUI, perform the following from the vSphere web client: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand System. 3. Select Advanced System Settings then click Edit. 4. Enter DCUI.Access in the filter. 5. Set the DCUI.Access attribute is set to a comma-separated list of the users who are allowed to override lockdown mode.

title: Host must have an accurate Exception Users list
description: Establishing an accurate Exception Users list is essential for managing user privileges during lockdown mode. Users on this list retain their privileges, making it imperative to include only those necessary for direct host access like service accounts for third-party solutions. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 3.19 Host must have an accurate Exception Users list

audit.command: To verify the membership of the "Exception Users" list, perform the following in the vSphere Web Client: 1. Select the host. 2. Click on Configure then expand System and select Security Profile. 3. Under Lockdown Mode view and verify the list of Exception Users for accuracy.

remediation.command: To correct the membership of the Exception Users list, perform the following in the vSphere Web Client: 1. Select the host. 2. Click on Configure then expand System and select Security Profile. 3. Select Edit next to Lockdown Mode. 4. Click on Exception Users. 5. Add or delete users as appropriate. 6. Click OK.

title: Host must deny shell access for the dcui account
description: The dcui account, utilized for process isolation for the Direct Console User Interface (DCUI), possesses shell access which, when deactivated, minimizes the attack surface. This action is a proactive measure to enhance system security. The audit runs esxcli system account list and requires Shell Access false for dcui. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 3.22 Host must deny shell access for the dcui account

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system account list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="dcui" {print tolower($NF); exit}')
case "$v" in false) echo compliant ;; '') echo 'dcui not listed (or no Shell Access column on this build)'; exit 1 ;; *) echo 'dcui shell access: '"$v" ;; esac

remediation.command: Configure the dcui service account to have no shell access using the supported ESXi account-management mechanism for the installed build, and verify that the account cannot establish an interactive shell. Note: It is advised not to manually edit /etc/passwd unless directed by Broadcom support.

title: Host must display a login banner for the DCUI and Host Client
description: Enabling a login banner on the Direct Console User Interface (DCUI) and the Host Client interfaces provides a mechanism to display legal notices or organizational announcements at login. The parameter governing this behavior is Annotations.WelcomeMessage, with the recommended value being a text string aligned with organizational or legal advisories. The audit reads Annotations.WelcomeMessage with esxcli and requires a non-empty banner; confirm the text matches the approved legal notice. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 3.24 Host must display a login banner for the DCUI and Host Client

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Annotations/WelcomeMessage 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *String Value: *//p' | head -n 1)
if [ -n "$v" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Annotations/WelcomeMessage = '$v' (empty banner)"; fi

remediation.command: Set the approved banner using Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name Annotations.WelcomeMessage | Set-AdvancedSetting -Value '<approved banner>' - Confirm:$false, or configure it in Host > Configure > System > Advanced System Settings. Verify it displays in DCUI/Host Client.

title: Host must display a login banner for SSH connections
description: ESXi facilitates the display of a login message, primarily aimed to deter unauthorized access and inform legitimate users regarding system usage obligations, particularly during SSH connections. The text for this display is defined by a specific parameter, which is advisable to be configured, especially when SSH is active, albeit it's recommended to keep SSH in a stopped state ... The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires a Banner directive pointing to a non-empty file. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 3.25 Host must display a login banner for SSH connections

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
b=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="banner" {print $2; exit}' "$f")
case "$b" in ''|none) echo 'no SSH Banner configured'; exit 1 ;; esac
[ -s "$b" ] && echo compliant || echo "banner file $b is missing or empty"

remediation.guidance: 1. Configure Banner /etc/issue in the SSH configuration and place the approved warning text in the referenced file. 2. Restart SSH only if it is authorized to be running; otherwise leave SSH disabled.

title: Host must enable the highest version of TLS supported
description: The host should be configured to operate using the highest version of TLS supported to ensure secure communications. ESXi 8, by default, comes with TLS 1.2 enabled, although re-enabling other protocols is possible if required. Employing the highest version of TLS aids in protecting against known vulnerabilities present in older versions. The audit reads UserVars.ESXiVPsDisabledProtocols with esxcli and requires sslv3, tlsv1 and tlsv1.1 to be listed. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 3.26 Host must enable the highest version of TLS supported

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /UserVars/ESXiVPsDisabledProtocols 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s
' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *String Value: *//p' | head -n 1)
if printf "%s" "$v" | tr "A-Z" "a-z" | tr -d " " | tr "," "
" | grep -qx sslv3 && printf "%s" "$v" | tr "A-Z" "a-z" | tr -d " " | tr "," "
" | grep -qx tlsv1 && printf "%s" "$v" | tr "A-Z" "a-z" | tr -d " " | tr "," "
" | grep -qx "tlsv1[.]1"; then echo compliant; else echo "/UserVars/ESXiVPsDisabledProtocols = '$v' (expected sslv3,tlsv1,tlsv1.1 disabled)"; fi

remediation.guidance: Disable unsupported/legacy protocol versions using Broadcom-supported TLS configuration procedures for ESXi 8 and dependent services. Test vCenter, backup, monitoring, and API integrations before broad deployment.

title: Host must configure a persistent log location for all locally stored system logs
description: Configure the Syslog.global.logDir parameter to specify a persistent directory for system logs, ensuring they are retained across reboots. This can be set to a directory on mounted NFS or VMFS volumes, other than the default which is an in-memory filesystem that retains only a single day's worth of logs. The audit runs esxcli system syslog config get and requires "Local Log Output Is Persistent: true". Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.1 Host must configure a persistent log location for all locally stored system logs

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system syslog config get 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -F': *' 'tolower($1) ~ /^ *local log output is persistent$/ {print $2; exit}' | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | sed 's/ *$//')
if [ "$v" = true ]; then echo compliant; else echo "Local Log Output Is Persistent: ${v:-not reported}"; fi

remediation.command: To configure persistent logging properly, perform the following from the vSphere web client: 1. Select the host 2. Click Configure then expand System then select Advanced System Settings. 3. Select Edit then enter Syslog.global.LogDir in the filter. 4. Set Syslog.global.logDir to a persistent location specified as [datastorename] path_to_file where the path is relative to the datastore. For example, [datastore1] /systemlogs. 5. Click OK. Alternatively, run the following PowerCLI command: # Set Syslog.global.logDir for each host Get-VMHost | Foreach { Set-AdvancedConfiguration -VMHost $_ -Name Syslog.global.logDir -Value "<NewLocation>" }

title: Host must transmit system logs to a remote log collector
description: Transmitting system logs to a remote log collector ensures that ESXi logs are stored in a secure and centralized manner. This centralization not only allows for the streamlined monitoring of all hosts through a single tool but also facilitates aggregate analysis and searching capabilities. The audit reads Syslog.global.logHost with esxcli and requires it to be set. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.2 Host must transmit system logs to a remote log collector

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/logHost 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *String Value: *//p' | head -n 1)
[ -n "$v" ] && echo compliant || echo 'Syslog.global.logHost is empty'

remediation.command: To configure remote logging properly, perform the following from the vSphere web client: 1. Select the host 2. Click Configure then expand System then select Advanced System Settings. 3. Select Edit then enter Syslog.global.logHost in the filter. 4. Set the Syslog.global.logHost to the hostname or IP address of the central log server. 5. Click OK. Alternately, run the following PowerCLI command: # Set Syslog.global.logHost for each host Get-VMHost | Foreach { Set-AdvancedSetting -VMHost $_ -Name Syslog.global.logHost -Value "<NewLocation>" } Note: When setting a remote log host, it is also recommended to set the "Syslog.global.logDirUnique" to true.

title: Host must log sufficient information for events
description: Set the Syslog.global.logLevel parameter to "info" to ensure that audit logs capture sufficient information for diagnosing issues and investigating security events. This setting strikes a balance between log verbosity and storage utilization. The parameter governing this behavior is Syslog.global.logLevel with a recommended setting of info. The audit reads Syslog.global.logLevel with esxcli and requires info; also review logger rotation/size (esxcli system syslog config logger list). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.3 Host must log sufficient information for events

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/logLevel 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *String Value: *//p' | head -n 1)
if [ "$v" = info ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Syslog/global/logLevel = '$v' (expected info)"; fi

remediation.guidance: 1. Increase the number of rotations and/or individual log size 2. esxcli system syslog config logger set --id=vmkernel --rotate=15 --size=10240 3. esxcli system syslog config logger set --id=hostd --rotate=15 -- size=10240

title: Host must set the logging informational level to info
description: Set the logging informational level to "info" via the Config.HostAgent.log.level parameter to ensure audit logs contain adequate data for diagnostics and forensics. This level provides a balanced amount of detail, suitable for routine analysis and investigation. The parameter governing this behavior is Config.HostAgent.log.level with a recommended setting of info. The audit reads Config.HostAgent.log.level with esxcli and requires info. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.4 Host must set the logging informational level to info

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Config/HostAgent/log/level 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *String Value: *//p' | head -n 1)
if [ "$v" = info ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Config/HostAgent/log/level = '$v' (expected info)"; fi

remediation.guidance: Using the vSphere client: Host → Configure → System → Advanced System Settings → Syslog.global.logLevel Set: info Execute command: esxcli system syslog config get | grep "Log Level" Verify - Log Level: info

title: Host must deactivate log filtering
description: Log filtering can be employed to diminish the frequency of repetitive log entries and to preclude specific log events entirely. By employing the Syslog.global.logFilters configuration parameter, one can stipulate filtering criteria, which when met, will cause the designated log events to be excluded from the system logs. The audit reads Syslog.global.logFiltersEnable with esxcli and requires false (0). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.5 Host must deactivate log filtering

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/logFiltersEnable 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Syslog/global/logFiltersEnable: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Syslog/global/logFiltersEnable = $v (expected false/0)"; fi

remediation.guidance: 1. Disable log filtering 2. execute command: esxcli system syslog config logfilter set --log- filtering-enabled=false 3. execute: Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name "Syslog.global.logFiltersEnable" passing value is: False

title: Host must enable audit record logging
description: Enabling audit record logging on ESXi hosts ensures the local storage of audit records, providing a trail of activities performed on the host. This measure is pivotal for accountability, troubleshooting, and security investigations. The parameter governing this behavior is Syslog.global.auditRecord.storageEnable with a recommended setting of TRUE. The audit reads Syslog.global.auditRecord.storageEnable with esxcli and requires true (1). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.6 Host must enable audit record logging

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/auditRecord/storageEnable 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Syslog/global/auditRecord/storageEnable: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Syslog/global/auditRecord/storageEnable = $v (expected true/1)"; fi

remediation.guidance: To enable local audit-record logging: 1. Execute command: esxcli system auditrecords local enable 2. Verify remediation with: esxcli system auditrecords get 3. passing results: Audit Record Storage Active: true

title: Host must configure a persistent log location for all locally stored audit records
description: Configuring a persistent log location for locally stored audit records on ESXi hosts is critical to ensure audit continuity. When the "/scratch" directory is linked to "/tmp/scratch", only a day's worth of records are retained, and they are reinitialized upon each reboot, creating a security risk. The audit reads Syslog.global.auditRecord.storageDirectory with esxcli and requires a datastore path (/vmfs/volumes/... or [datastore] ...); the default /scratch location fails. Do not use a vSAN datastore. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.7 Host must configure a persistent log location for all locally stored audit records

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/auditRecord/storageDirectory 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *String Value: *//p' | head -n 1)
if case "$v" in /vmfs/volumes/?*|\[*\]*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; then echo compliant; else echo "/Syslog/global/auditRecord/storageDirectory = '$v' (expected a persistent datastore path)"; fi

remediation.command: Configure a persistent datastore location with: esxcli system auditrecords local set \ -- directory=/vmfs/volumes/<Datastore-UUID>/audit/<hostname> then esxcli system auditrecords local enable verify compliance with: esxcli system auditrecords get compliant results = Audit Record Storage Active: true Audit Record Storage Directory: /vmfs/volumes/<Datastore-UUID>/audit/<hostname>

title: Host must store one week of audit records
description: Ensuring a local storage capacity for a week's worth of audit records is imperative, especially when a remote audit record storage facility is used. This provision is critical during anticipated interruptions in record delivery to the remote facility, preventing loss or overwriting of audit records. The audit reads Syslog.global.auditRecord.storageCapacity (MiB) with esxcli and requires the recommended 100 or more; confirm it holds 7 days of records. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.8 Host must store one week of audit records

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/auditRecord/storageCapacity 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Syslog/global/auditRecord/storageCapacity: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -ge 100 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Syslog/global/auditRecord/storageCapacity = $v (expected 100 or more)"; fi

remediation.guidance: Increase the local audit-record storage capacity to store at least 7 days worth of audit logs. execute: esxcli system auditrecords local set --size=<MiB>

title: Host must transmit audit records to a remote log collector
description: This control enables the forwarding of audit records from the ESXi host to a designated log collector, aiding in real-time monitoring and analysis. The parameter governing this behavior is Syslog.global.auditRecord.remoteEnable with a recommended setting of TRUE. The audit requires Syslog.global.logHost to be set and Syslog.global.auditRecord.remoteEnable to be true (1). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.9 Host must transmit audit records to a remote log collector

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/logHost 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *String Value: *//p' | head -n 1)
[ -n "$v" ] || { echo 'Syslog.global.logHost is empty'; exit 1; }
out2=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/auditRecord/remoteEnable 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out2" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Syslog/global/auditRecord/remoteEnable: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Syslog/global/auditRecord/remoteEnable = $v (expected true/1)"; fi

remediation.command: To configure remote logging properly, perform the following from the vSphere web client: 1. Select the host 2. Click Configure then expand System then select Advanced System Settings. 3. Select Edit then enter Syslog.global.logHost in the filter. 4. Set the Syslog.global.logHost to the hostname or IP address of the central log server. 5. Click OK. Alternately, run the following PowerCLI command: # Set Syslog.global.logHost for each host Get-VMHost | Foreach { Set-AdvancedSetting -VMHost $_ -Name Syslog.global.logHost -Value "<NewLocation>" } Note: When setting a remote log host, it is also recommended to set the "Syslog.global.logDirUnique" to true.

title: Host must verify certificates for TLS remote logging endpoints
description: When engaging in remote logging activities, it is of utmost importance to ensure that the logging endpoint is genuine and secure. To achieve this, hosts should verify the TLS certificates of these endpoints. This verification provides assurance that the endpoint is both authentic and trustworthy, mitigating the risk of transmitting logs to potentially malicious or untrusted ... The audit reads Syslog.global.certificate.checkSSLCerts with esxcli and requires true (1). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.10 Host must verify certificates for TLS remote logging endpoints

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/certificate/checkSSLCerts 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Syslog/global/certificate/checkSSLCerts: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Syslog/global/certificate/checkSSLCerts = $v (expected true/1)"; fi

remediation.guidance: Execute command: esxcli system syslog config set --check-ssl-certs=true Verify with: esxcli system syslog config get remediated result should include: ssl://

title: Host must use strict x509 verification for TLS-enabled remote logging endpoints
description: When employing remote logging with TLS-enabled endpoints, it is essential to ensure the utmost integrity and authenticity of the certificates in use. The "x509-strict" option provides a higher level of security by performing additional validity checks on CA root certificates during the verification process. The audit reads Syslog.global.certificate.strictX509Compliance with esxcli and requires true (1). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 4.11 Host must use strict x509 verification for TLS-enabled remote logging endpoints

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Syslog/global/certificate/strictX509Compliance 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Syslog/global/certificate/strictX509Compliance: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Syslog/global/certificate/strictX509Compliance = $v (expected true/1)"; fi

remediation.guidance: Utilize PowerCLI to remediate </> Powershell Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name "Syslog.global.certificate.strictX509Compliance" | Set-AdvancedSetting -Value $true -Confirm:$false Verify with Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name "Syslog.global.certificate.strictX509Compliance" Expected Calue is: Value = True

title: Host must block network traffic by default
description: By default, the host is configured to block all incoming and outgoing network traffic, except for the traffic pertaining to services enabled in the host security profile. This configuration is pivotal in reducing the attack surface and averting unauthorized access to the host. The audit runs esxcli network firewall get and requires "Enabled: true" and "Default Action: DROP"; review enabled rulesets as well. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.2 Host must block network traffic by default

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli network firewall get 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
a=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *Default Action: *//p' | head -n 1)
e=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *Enabled: *//p' | head -n 1)
[ "$a" = DROP ] && [ "$e" = true ] && echo compliant || echo "firewall enabled=$e default action=$a"

remediation.command: 1. Enable the ESXi firewall if disabled and disable unnecessary rulesets. 2. Use: esxcli network firewall set --enabled true 3. Configure only the required rulesets for documented services.

title: Host must restrict use of the dvFilter network API
description: The Net.DVFilterBindIpAddress parameter controls the use of the dvFilter network API, allowing network information to be sent to a specified IP address. If enabled with a compromised IP address, unauthorized network access to other virtual machines on the host could occur. It's essential to keep this parameter unconfigured, unless required by a product like VMware NSX. The audit reads Net.DVFilterBindIpAddress with esxcli and requires an empty value (set it only when a dvfilter security appliance is used). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.3 Host must restrict use of the dvFilter network API

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Net/DVFilterBindIpAddress 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *String Value: *//p' | head -n 1)
if [ -z "$v" ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Net/DVFilterBindIpAddress = '$v' (expected empty)"; fi

remediation.guidance: To remove the configuration for the dvfilter network API, perform the following from the vSphere web client: 1. From the vSphere web client, select the host and click Configure then expand System 2. Click on Advanced System Settings then Edit. 3. Search for Net.DVFilterBindIpAddress in the filter. 4. Set Net.DVFilterBindIpAddress has an empty value. 5. If an appliance is being used, make sure the value of this parameter is set to the proper IP address. 6. Enter the proper IP address. 7. Click OK.

title: Host must filter Bridge Protocol Data Unit (BPDU) packets
description: To prevent cascading lockout of uplink interfaces from the ESXi host, the Net.BlockGuestBPDU parameter can be set to 1, enabling BPDU Filter to drop BPDU packets sent from virtual machines to the physical switch. This is crucial as ESXi's Standard and Distributed Virtual Switches do not support STP, making them prone to network loops if BPDUs are unfiltered. The audit reads Net.BlockGuestBPDU with esxcli and requires 1. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.4 Host must filter Bridge Protocol Data Unit (BPDU) packets

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Net/BlockGuestBPDU 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Net/BlockGuestBPDU: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Net/BlockGuestBPDU = $v (expected 1)"; fi

remediation.guidance: From an administrative PowerCLI session: Execute - Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name Net.BlockGuestBPDU | Set- AdvancedSetting -Value 1 -Confirm:$false. Validate network appliances/virtual switching workloads before enforcing this setting.

title: Host should reject forged transmits on standard virtual switches and port groups
description: Setting the "Forged transmits" option to "Reject" helps prevent MAC impersonation by comparing the source MAC address from the guest operating system with the effective MAC address of its virtual machine adapter. If there's a mismatch, the packet is dropped, preventing potential malicious activities through impersonated MAC addresses. The audit runs esxcli network vswitch standard (portgroup) policy security get for every standard vSwitch and port group and requires "Allow Forged Transmits: false". Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.6 Host should reject forged transmits on standard virtual switches and port groups

audit.command:
command -v esxcli >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
vs=$(esxcli network vswitch standard list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Name: *//p') || exit 1
pgs=$(esxcli --formatter=csv network vswitch standard portgroup list 2>/dev/null | awk -F, 'NR==1 {for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == "Name") c = i; next} c {print $c}') || exit 1
out=$(for v in $vs; do
  x=$(esxcli network vswitch standard policy security get -v "$v" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Allow Forged Transmits: *//p' | head -n 1)
  [ "$x" = false ] || echo "vSwitch $v: Allow Forged Transmits=${x:-unknown}"
done
printf '%s\n' "$pgs" | while IFS= read -r p; do [ -n "$p" ] || continue
  x=$(esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup policy security get -p "$p" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Allow Forged Transmits: *//p' | head -n 1)
  [ "$x" = false ] || echo "portgroup $p: Allow Forged Transmits=${x:-unknown}"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: To set the policy to reject forged transmissions, perform the following: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand Networking. 3. Select Virtual switches then click Edit. 4. Click on Security. 5. Set Forged transmits to Reject in the dropdown. 6. Click on OK. Alternately, the following ESXi shell command may be used: # esxcli network vswitch standard policy security set -v vSwitch2 -f false

title: Host should reject MAC address changes on standard virtual switches and port groups
description: Enforcing MAC address stability on standard virtual switches and port groups prevents MAC impersonation by disallowing changes to the MAC address by virtual machines. This mitigates the risk of malicious activities initiated by impersonating authorized network adapters. The audit runs esxcli network vswitch standard (portgroup) policy security get for every standard vSwitch and port group and requires "Allow MAC Address Change: false". Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.7 Host should reject MAC address changes on standard virtual switches and port groups

audit.command:
command -v esxcli >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
vs=$(esxcli network vswitch standard list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Name: *//p') || exit 1
pgs=$(esxcli --formatter=csv network vswitch standard portgroup list 2>/dev/null | awk -F, 'NR==1 {for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == "Name") c = i; next} c {print $c}') || exit 1
out=$(for v in $vs; do
  x=$(esxcli network vswitch standard policy security get -v "$v" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Allow MAC Address Change: *//p' | head -n 1)
  [ "$x" = false ] || echo "vSwitch $v: Allow MAC Address Change=${x:-unknown}"
done
printf '%s\n' "$pgs" | while IFS= read -r p; do [ -n "$p" ] || continue
  x=$(esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup policy security get -p "$p" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Allow MAC Address Change: *//p' | head -n 1)
  [ "$x" = false ] || echo "portgroup $p: Allow MAC Address Change=${x:-unknown}"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: To set the policy to reject, perform the following: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand Networking. 3. Select Virtual switches then click Edit. 4. Click on Security. 5. Set MAC address changes to Reject in the dropdown. 6. Click on OK. Alternately, perform the following using the ESXi shell: # esxcli network vswitch standard policy security set -v vSwitch2 -m false

title: Host should reject promiscuous mode requests on standard virtual switches and port groups
description: Enabling promiscuous mode allows all virtual machines in a port group to read all packets transmitted across it, regardless of the intended recipient. Rejecting promiscuous mode requests on standard virtual switches and port groups prevents unauthorized packet inspection, enhancing network isolation and data privacy. The audit runs esxcli network vswitch standard (portgroup) policy security get for every standard vSwitch and port group and requires "Allow Promiscuous: false". Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.8 Host should reject promiscuous mode requests on standard virtual switches and port groups

audit.command:
command -v esxcli >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
vs=$(esxcli network vswitch standard list 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Name: *//p') || exit 1
pgs=$(esxcli --formatter=csv network vswitch standard portgroup list 2>/dev/null | awk -F, 'NR==1 {for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == "Name") c = i; next} c {print $c}') || exit 1
out=$(for v in $vs; do
  x=$(esxcli network vswitch standard policy security get -v "$v" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Allow Promiscuous: *//p' | head -n 1)
  [ "$x" = false ] || echo "vSwitch $v: Allow Promiscuous=${x:-unknown}"
done
printf '%s\n' "$pgs" | while IFS= read -r p; do [ -n "$p" ] || continue
  x=$(esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup policy security get -p "$p" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Allow Promiscuous: *//p' | head -n 1)
  [ "$x" = false ] || echo "portgroup $p: Allow Promiscuous=${x:-unknown}"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: To set the policy to reject, perform the following: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand Networking. 3. Select Virtual switches then click Edit. 4. Click on Security. 5. Set Promiscuous mode to Reject in the dropdown. 6. Click on OK. Alternately, perform the following via the ESXi shell: # esxcli network vswitch standard policy security set -v vSwitch2 -p false

title: Host must restrict access to a default or native VLAN on standard virtual switches
description: ESXi does not use the concept of native VLAN, so do not configure port groups to use the native VLAN ID. If the default value of 1 for the native VLAN is being used, the ESXi Server virtual switch port groups should be configured with any value between 2 and 4094. Otherwise, ensure that the port group is not configured to use whatever value is set for the native VLAN. The audit lists standard port groups (esxcli --formatter=csv network vswitch standard portgroup list) and fails any using VLAN ID 1, the usual default/native VLAN; adjust if your physical switches use another native VLAN. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.9 Host must restrict access to a default or native VLAN on standard virtual switches

remediation.command: To stop using the native VLAN ID for port groups, perform the following: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand Networking. 3. Select Virtual switches. 4. Expand the Standard vSwitch. 5. View the topology diagram of the switch, which shows the various port groups associated with that switch. 6. For each port group on the vSwitch, verify and record the VLAN IDs used. 7. If a VLAN ID change is needed, click the name of the port group in the topology diagram of the virtual switch. 8. Click the Edit settings option. 9. In the Properties section, enter an appropriate name in the Network label field. 10. In the VLAN ID dropdown select or type a new VLAN.

title: Host must restrict the use of Virtual Guest Tagging (VGT) on standard virtual switches
description: When a port group is set to VLAN 4095 on standard virtual switches, it enables Virtual Guest Tagging (VGT), letting all network frames pass to the attached virtual machines (VMs) without altering the VLAN tags. This requires VMs to process VLAN information themselves via an 802.1Q driver. The audit lists standard port groups and fails any using VLAN ID 4095 (Virtual Guest Tagging); document the exception when VGT is required. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.10 Host must restrict the use of Virtual Guest Tagging (VGT) on standard virtual switches

remediation.command: To set port groups to values other than 4095 and 0 unless VGT is required, perform the following: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand Networking. 3. Select Virtual switches. 4. Expand the Standard vSwitch. 5. View the topology diagram of the switch, which shows the various port groups associated with that switch. 6. For each port group on the vSwitch, verify and record the VLAN IDs used. 7. If a VLAN ID change is needed, click the name of the port group in the topology diagram of the virtual switch. 8. Click the Edit settings option. 9. In the Properties section, enter an appropriate name in the Network label field. 10.

title: Host must isolate management communications
description: Ensure that only vmk interfaces designated for management purposes have management services enabled to uphold network isolation and security. Incorrect configuration may undermine security efforts by breaching network isolation principles. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.11 Host must isolate management communications

audit.command: Review VMkernel adapters with: esxcli network ip interface list Verify that management traffic is carried only on dedicated, approved VMkernel interfaces/VLANs and is not mixed with untrusted VM, storage, vMotion, or public traffic without an approved design.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, create or move management VMkernel interfaces to dedicated management port groups/VLANs, apply firewall/ACL restrictions, and remove management service flags from interfaces that do not require them. Test vCenter connectivity before deleting the old path.

title: Host CIM services, if enabled, must limit access
description: The Common Information Model (CIM) system allows for hardware-level management from remote applications through standard APIs. Ensuring only minimal access necessary to these applications is imperative to prevent potential security compromises. A dedicated service account, specific to each CIM application, should be created to limit access and privileges. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.1.1 Host CIM services, if enabled, must limit access

audit.command: To verify CIM access is limited, check for a limited-privileged service account with the following CIM roles applied: Host.Config.SystemManagement Host.CIM.CIMInteraction Alternately, the following PowerCLI command may be used: # List all user accounts on the Host -Host Local connection required- Get-VMHostAccount

remediation.command: To limit CIM access, perform the following: 1. Create a limited-privileged service account for CIM and other third-party applications. 2. This account should access the system via vCenter. 3. Give the account the CIM Interaction privilege only. This will enable the account to obtain a CIM ticket, which can then be used to perform both read and write CIM operations on the target host. If an account must connect to the host directly, this account must be granted the full "Administrator" role on the host. This is not recommended unless required by the monitoring software being used.

title: Host must isolate storage communications
description: Isolating storage communications through zoning and Logical Unit Number (LUN) masking is instrumental in segregating Storage Area Network (SAN) activity. Zoning defines the connections between host bus adapters (HBAs) and targets, ensuring devices outside a zone remain invisible to the devices within, thus facilitating the independent management of zones such as testing and ... Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.2.1 Host must isolate storage communications

audit.command: The audit procedures to verify SAN activity is properly segregated are SAN vendor or product-specific.

remediation.command: The remediation procedures to properly segregate SAN activity are SAN vendor or product-specific. In general, with ESXi hosts, use a single-initiator zoning or a single-initiator-single-target zoning. The latter is a preferred zoning practice. Using the more restrictive zoning prevents problems and misconfigurations that can occur on the SAN.

title: Host must ensure all datastores have unique names
description: Ensuring unique naming for datastores is crucial to avoid potential errors that could affect the integrity and availability of data. A descriptive and unique name for each datastore facilitates better identification and management. Although there's no specific parameter to enforce this, manual or automated naming conventions should be adhered to. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.2.2 Host must ensure all datastores have unique names

audit.command: List datastores with: esxcli storage filesystem list or PowerCLI Get-Datastore Verify that datastore names are unique across the managed vCenter inventory and are descriptive enough to prevent administrative ambiguity.

remediation.command: See the CIS benchmark remediation procedure.

title: Host iSCSI client, if enabled, must employ bidirectional/mutual CHAP authentication
description: Implementing bidirectional CHAP authentication for iSCSI connections elevates security by necessitating mutual verification between the initiator (client) and target (server), ensuring data integrity during transmission. Configuration involves setting the iSCSI storage adapter authentication to "Use bidirectional CHAP" and providing the requisite credentials. The audit lists iSCSI adapters (esxcli iscsi adapter list) and requires CHAP level "required" in both uni and mutual directions on each; with no iSCSI adapters the rule passes. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.3.1 Host iSCSI client, if enabled, must employ bidirectional/mutual CHAP authentication

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli iscsi adapter list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
ad=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk 'NR > 2 && $1 ~ /^vmhba/ {print $1}')
bad=''
for a in $ad; do
  u=$(esxcli iscsi adapter auth chap get -A "$a" -d uni 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Level: *//p' | head -n 1)
  m=$(esxcli iscsi adapter auth chap get -A "$a" -d mutual 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *Level: *//p' | head -n 1)
  [ "$u" = required ] && [ "$m" = required ] || bad="$bad $a(uni=${u:-?},mutual=${m:-?})"
done
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || echo "iSCSI adapters without bidirectional CHAP:$bad"

remediation.command: To enable bidirectional CHAP authentication for iSCSI traffic, perform the following: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand Storage. 3. Select Storage Adapters then select the iSCSI Adapter. 4. Under Properties click on Edit next to Authentication. 5. Next to Authentication Method select Use bidirectional CHAP from the dropdown. 6. Specify the outgoing CHAP name. ; Make sure that the name you specify matches the name configured on the storage side. o To set the CHAP name to the iSCSI adapter name, select "Use initiator name".

title: Host iSCSI client, if enabled, must employ unique CHAP authentication secrets
description: Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol (CHAP) requires both client and host to know a secret to establish a connection. It is essential to employ unique CHAP authentication secrets for each iSCSI session to ensure secure communications. The parameter governing this behavior is outlined in the iSCSI or iSER storage adapter configuration under CHAP settings. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.3.2 Host iSCSI client, if enabled, must employ unique CHAP authentication secrets

audit.command: To verify the CHAP secrets are unique, run the following to list all iSCSI adapters and their corresponding CHAP configuration: # List Iscsi Initiator and CHAP Name if defined Get-VMHost | Get-VMHostHba | Where {$_.Type -eq "Iscsi"} | Select VMHost, Device, ChapType, @{N="CHAPName";E={$_.AuthenticationProperties.ChapName}}

remediation.command: To change the values of CHAP secrets so they are unique, perform the following: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Click Configure then expand Storage. 3. Select Storage Adapters then select the iSCSI Adapter. 4. Under Properties click on Edit next to Authentication. 5. Next to Authentication Method specify the authentication method from the dropdown. o None o Use unidirectional CHAP if required by target o Use unidirectional CHAP unless prohibited by target o Use unidirectional CHAP o Use bidirectional CHAP 6. Specify the outgoing CHAP name. ; Make sure that the name you specify matches the name configured on the storage side.

title: Host SNMP services, if enabled, must limit access
description: To manage hosts securely, if SNMP is enabled, access must be restricted. Preferably, SNMPv3 should be employed as it offers superior security through key authentication and encryption compared to SNMPv1 or SNMPv2. Configuring the destination for SNMP traps is essential for ensuring monitoring data is directed to a legitimate and secure host. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.4.1 Host SNMP services, if enabled, must limit access

audit.command: To confirm the proper configuration of SNMP, perform the following from the ESXi Shell or vCLI: 1. Run the following to determine if SNMP is being used: esxcli system snmp get 2. If SNMP is being used, refer to the vSphere Monitoring and Performance guide, chapter 8 for steps to verify the parameters. Additionally, the following PowerCLI command may be used to view the SNMP configuration: # List the SNMP Configuration of a host (single host connection required) Get-VMHostSnmp

remediation.command: To correct the SNMP configuration, perform the following from the ESXi Shell or vCLI: 1. If SNMP is not needed, disable it by running: esxcli system snmp set --enable false 2. If SNMP is needed, refer to the vSphere Monitoring and Performance guide, chapter 8 for steps to configure it. Additionally, the following PowerCLI command may be used to implement the configuration: # Update the host SNMP Configuration (single host connection required) Get-VmHostSNMP | Set-VMHostSNMP -Enabled:$true -ReadOnlyCommunity '<secret>' Notes: ; SNMP must be configured on each ESXi host ; SNMP settings can be configured using Host Profiles

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must use FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated ciphers
description: For enhanced security, if the SSH daemon is enabled on the host, it must utilize FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated ciphers. This requirement ensures the encryption standards are robust and compliant with regulatory mandates. The audit reads the Ciphers directive of /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires only AES-based (FIPS-approved) ciphers. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.1 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must use FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated ciphers

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
c=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="ciphers" {print tolower($2); exit}' "$f")
[ -n "$c" ] || { echo 'Ciphers not set explicitly'; exit 1; }
bad=$(printf '%s\n' "$c" | tr ',' '\n' | grep -v '^aes' | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -z "$bad" ] && echo compliant || echo "non-FIPS ciphers: $bad"

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, configure the SSH daemon to use only the approved FIPS-capable cipher list supported by the installed ESXi build. Validate access from approved administration clients before deploying broadly.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must use FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptographic modules
description: When enabled, the SSH daemon on the host should employ FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptographic modules provided by OpenSSH. Although these modules are enabled by default, they can be deactivated for backward compatibility, thus auditing and ensuring the correct setting is crucial for maintaining security standards. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.2 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must use FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptographic modules

audit.command: Verify ESXi is operating with Broadcom-supported cryptographic modules and that SSH is using the platform-provided OpenSSH/crypto libraries. Review installed VIBs and do not accept replacement third-party SSH/crypto binaries.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, remove unsupported SSH/cryptographic binaries and restore the signed ESXi components from an approved image/profile. Keep ESXi patched so the validated cryptographic modules remain current.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must not allow use of gateway ports
description: When enabled, the SSH daemon on the host should have the gateway ports feature disabled to prevent remote hosts from forwarding connections. This is a hardening measure to ensure that the SSH service is securely configured against potential forwarding misuses. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires GatewayPorts no (unset = OpenSSH default no). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.3 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must not allow use of gateway ports

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="gatewayports" {print tolower($2); exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in '') echo compliant ;; no) echo compliant ;; *) echo "GatewayPorts $v" ;; esac

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set GatewayPorts no in the supported ESXi SSH configuration. Restart SSH only during an authorized maintenance/admin window and verify the effective setting.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must not allow host-based authentication
description: Ensuring the SSH daemon on the host disallows host-based authentication is a crucial step towards hardening system services. This prevents a host from authenticating on behalf of the users, thereby enforcing individual accountability and minimizing the risk of unauthorized access. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires HostbasedAuthentication no (unset = OpenSSH default no). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.4 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must not allow host-based authentication

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="hostbasedauthentication" {print tolower($2); exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in '') echo compliant ;; no) echo compliant ;; *) echo "HostbasedAuthentication $v" ;; esac

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set HostbasedAuthentication no, restart SSH if it is authorized to run, and verify host-based authentication is rejected.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must set a timeout count on idle sessions
description: Setting a timeout count on idle SSH sessions ensures that inactive sessions are automatically disconnected after a specified period. This period is calculated by multiplying the timeout count with the idle timeout interval. Automatic disconnection of idle sessions reduces the window of opportunity for unauthorized access. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires ClientAliveCountMax to be set to a non-zero value; confirm it matches the approved value. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.5 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must set a timeout count on idle sessions

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="clientalivecountmax" {print $2; exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 'ClientAliveCountMax ${v:-not set}'; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$v" -gt 0 ] && echo compliant || echo 'ClientAliveCountMax is 0'

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set ClientAliveCountMax to the approved value, then restart SSH if enabled and test that inactive sessions are closed after the configured interval/count.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must set a timeout interval on idle sessions
description: Implementing a timeout interval on idle SSH sessions ensures that any inactive session gets disconnected after a certain period, improving the security posture. The total timeout duration is calculated by multiplying the timeout count by the idle timeout interval. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires ClientAliveInterval to be set to a non-zero number of seconds; confirm it matches the approved value. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.6 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must set a timeout interval on idle sessions

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="clientaliveinterval" {print $2; exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 'ClientAliveInterval ${v:-not set}'; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$v" -gt 0 ] && echo compliant || echo 'ClientAliveInterval is 0'

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set ClientAliveInterval to the approved number of seconds. Restart SSH if enabled and validate timeout behavior together with ClientAliveCountMax.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must display the system login banner before granting access
description: Implementing a system login banner before granting SSH access ensures that crucial information or notices are conveyed to users attempting to login. The banner text is set through the host's Config.Etc.Issue advanced parameter. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires a Banner directive pointing to a non-empty file. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.7 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must display the system login banner before granting access

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
b=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="banner" {print $2; exit}' "$f")
case "$b" in ''|none) echo 'no SSH Banner configured'; exit 1 ;; esac
[ -s "$b" ] && echo compliant || echo "banner file $b is missing or empty"

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, configure the approved SSH banner file and Banner directive. Restart SSH only if enabled/authorized and confirm the banner appears before authentication.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must ignore .rhosts files
description: Ignoring .rhosts files is crucial in hardening the SSH daemon on the host, ensuring that trust relationships are explicitly defined and not implicitly accepted, thereby reducing the attack surface. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires IgnoreRhosts yes (unset = OpenSSH default yes). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.8 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must ignore .rhosts files

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="ignorerhosts" {print tolower($2); exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in '') echo compliant ;; yes) echo compliant ;; *) echo "IgnoreRhosts $v" ;; esac

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set IgnoreRhosts yes, restart SSH if authorized, and verify .rhosts-based trust is ignored.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must disable stream local forwarding
description: Disabling stream local forwarding on the SSH daemon ensures that no Unix domain sockets are forwarded, thus enforcing a security boundary. This measure aids in maintaining the integrity and confidentiality of the system. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires AllowStreamLocalForwarding no. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.9 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must disable stream local forwarding

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="allowstreamlocalforwarding" {print tolower($2); exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in '') echo 'AllowStreamLocalForwarding not set' ;; no) echo compliant ;; *) echo "AllowStreamLocalForwarding $v" ;; esac

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set AllowStreamLocalForwarding no, restart SSH if authorized, and verify stream-local forwarding cannot be established.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must disable TCP forwarding
description: Disabling TCP forwarding in the SSH daemon is a measure to prevent potential unauthorized tunneling and forwarding activities that could lead to data leaks or unauthorized data access. This measure adds a layer of security to the SSH service when enabled, making the system more resilient against certain types of network attacks. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires AllowTcpForwarding no. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.10 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must disable TCP forwarding

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="allowtcpforwarding" {print tolower($2); exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in '') echo 'AllowTcpForwarding not set' ;; no) echo compliant ;; *) echo "AllowTcpForwarding $v" ;; esac

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set AllowTcpForwarding no, restart SSH if authorized, and test that TCP forwarding is blocked. Document any approved exception.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must not permit tunnels
description: Preventing tunnel creation in the SSH daemon is a security measure aimed at thwarting unauthorized network tunneling through the host. This control, when enforced, helps mitigate the risks associated with potential data exfiltration or unauthorized network access that could occur via SSH tunnels. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires PermitTunnel no (unset = OpenSSH default no). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.11 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must not permit tunnels

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="permittunnel" {print tolower($2); exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in '') echo compliant ;; no) echo compliant ;; *) echo "PermitTunnel $v" ;; esac

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set PermitTunnel no, restart SSH if authorized, and verify SSH tunnel devices cannot be created.

title: Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must not permit user environment settings
description: Preventing user environment settings in the SSH daemon ensures a consistent and controlled environment, reducing the attack surface by limiting the customization of the SSH environment by users. The audit reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config and requires PermitUserEnvironment no (unset = OpenSSH default no). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 6.5.12 Host SSH daemon, if enabled, must not permit user environment settings

audit.command:
f=/etc/ssh/sshd_config; [ -r "$f" ] || exit 1
v=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="permituserenvironment" {print tolower($2); exit}' "$f")
case "$v" in '') echo compliant ;; no) echo compliant ;; *) echo "PermitUserEnvironment $v" ;; esac

remediation.guidance: To remediate this recommendation, set PermitUserEnvironment no, restart SSH if authorized, and verify users cannot alter the SSH environment through per-user environment settings.

title: Virtual machines must require encryption for vMotion
description: Requiring encryption for vMotion ensures the secure transfer of data among virtual machines. While the default 'opportunistic' encryption setting generally provides encryption due to prevalent AES-NI support, enforcing 'required' encryption eradicates the possibility of unencrypted transfers. Expected: migrate.encryptionMode = "required". The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 7.2 Virtual machines must require encryption for vMotion

audit.command:
command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk -v KEYRE='^migrate[.]encryptionmode$' -v MODE='eq' -v VAL='required' 'BEGIN { re = tolower(KEYRE) }
{ line = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line); i = index(line, "="); if (i == 0) next
  k = tolower(substr(line, 1, i - 1)); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", k)
  v = substr(line, i + 1); sub(/^[ \t]*"?/, "", v); sub(/"?[ \t\r]*$/, "", v); v = tolower(v)
  if (k ~ re) { seen = 1; if (MODE == "not" && v == tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE != "not" && MODE != "ge" && v != tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE == "ge" && (v + 0) < (VAL + 0)) bad = bad " " k "=" v } }
END { if ((MODE == "eq" || MODE == "ge") && !seen) bad = " " KEYRE " not set"
      if (bad != "") print FILENAME ":" bad }' "$f"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.guidance: The following PowerCLI command may be used: $VMview = Get-VM -Name $VM | Get-View $ConfigSpec = New-Object VMware.Vim.VirtualMachineConfigSpec $ConfigSpec.MigrateEncryption = New-Object VMware.Vim.VirtualMachineConfigSpecEncryptedVMotionModes $ConfigSpec.MigrateEncryption = "required" $VMview.ReconfigVM_Task($ConfigSpec)

title: Virtual machines must require encryption for Fault Tolerance
description: Requiring encryption for Fault Tolerance in virtual machines is critical for ensuring secure data transmission between primary and secondary VMs, especially in environments where sensitive data is processed. While the default setting 'opportunistic' may result in encryption due to widespread AES-NI support in vSphere-compatible hardware, enforcing the 'required' setting for ... Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 7.3 Virtual machines must require encryption for Fault Tolerance

audit.command: The following PowerCLI command may be used: (Get-VM -Name $VM).ExtensionData.Config.FtEncryptionMode

remediation.command: The following PowerCLI command may be used: $VMview = Get-VM -Name $VM | Get-View $ConfigSpec = New-Object VMware.Vim.VirtualMachineConfigSpec $ConfigSpec.FtEncryptionMode = New-object VMware.Vim.VirtualMachineConfigSpecEncryptedFtModes $ConfigSpec.FtEncryptionMode = "ftEncryptionRequired" $VMview.ReconfigVM_Task($ConfigSpec)

title: Virtual machines must be configured to lock when the last console connection is closed
description: Configuring virtual machines to lock upon closing the last console connection enhances security by mitigating the risk of unauthorized access via open console sessions. This configuration is particularly useful in environments where multiple users have access to the console. Expected: tools.guest.desktop.autolock = "TRUE". The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 7.5 Virtual machines must be configured to lock when the last console connection is closed

audit.command:
command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk -v KEYRE='^tools[.]guest[.]desktop[.]autolock$' -v MODE='eq' -v VAL='TRUE' 'BEGIN { re = tolower(KEYRE) }

The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 7.19 Virtual machines must deactivate console paste operations

audit.command:
command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk -v KEYRE='^isolation[.]tools[.]paste[.]disable$' -v MODE='absent' -v VAL='TRUE' 'BEGIN { re = tolower(KEYRE) }
{ line = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line); i = index(line, "="); if (i == 0) next
  k = tolower(substr(line, 1, i - 1)); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", k)
  v = substr(line, i + 1); sub(/^[ \t]*"?/, "", v); sub(/"?[ \t\r]*$/, "", v); v = tolower(v)
  if (k ~ re) { seen = 1; if (MODE == "not" && v == tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE != "not" && MODE != "ge" && v != tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE == "ge" && (v + 0) < (VAL + 0)) bad = bad " " k "=" v } }
END { if ((MODE == "eq" || MODE == "ge") && !seen) bad = " " KEYRE " not set"
      if (bad != "") print FILENAME ":" bad }' "$f"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.guidance: To set this configuration utilize the vSphere interface as follows: 1. Select the VM then select Actions followed by Edit Settings. 2. Click on the VM Options tab then expand Advanced. 3. Click on EDIT CONFIGURATION. 4. Click on ADD CONFIGURATION PARAMS then input isolation.tools.paste.disable with a value of TRUE. 5. Click OK, then OK again. To explicitly disable VM console paste operations, run the following PowerCLI command: # Add the setting to all VMs Get-VM | New-AdvancedSetting -Name "isolation.tools.paste.disable" -value $true

title: VMware Tools must be a version that has not reached End of General Support status
description: Ensuring VMware Tools is running a version that has not reached its End of General Support (EOGS) status is imperative for maintaining a secure and supported environment. A version within its support period guarantees regular updates, security patches, and vendor support. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.1 VMware Tools must be a version that has not reached End of General Support status

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within each applicable guest operating system, execute VMwareToolboxCmd.exe -v. Compare the installed VMware Tools version to Broadcom lifecycle/support information and verify it has not reached End of General Support.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, upgrade VMware Tools to a supported release using vSphere, the guest package manager/open-vm-tools, or an enterprise software deployment tool. Reboot the guest if required and verify the installed version.

title: VMware Tools must have all software updates installed
description: Ensuring that all software updates are installed on VMware Tools is crucial for maintaining a healthy and secure virtual environment. These updates provide essential drivers, enable effective management of guest operating systems, and offer features necessary for VM deployment and customization. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.2 VMware Tools must have all software updates installed

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Determine the installed VMware Tools version in each guest and compare it with the current approved security/update baseline. Review Broadcom security advisories for fixes applicable to that Tools release.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, install all approved VMware Tools updates using vSphere, open-vm-tools packages, or enterprise endpoint management. Reboot if required and verify the post-update version.

title: VMware Tools should configure automatic upgrades as appropriate for the environment
description: Automatic upgrades of VMware Tools can be managed via vSphere, ensuring VMware Tools versions remain current. This functionality is advisable unless alternative management and update mechanisms are in place. It is recommended to have automatic updates enabled to minimize administrative overhead and maintain up-to- date features and security patches. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.3 VMware Tools should configure automatic upgrades as appropriate for the environment

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Review each VM's VMware Tools upgrade policy in vSphere (Edit Settings > VM Options > VMware Tools) and the guest's package-management policy. Verify that automatic upgrade behavior matches the organization's approved change-management model.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, enable automatic VMware Tools upgrades only where appropriate, or configure a controlled centralized update process. In vSphere select the approved 'check and upgrade Tools during power cycling' behavior as appropriate for the environment.

title: VMware Tools must limit the automatic addition of features
description: Limit the automatic addition of features during VMware Tools upgrade processes to maintain the desired security profile of the guest operating system from vSphere. This control can be managed by setting the configuration parameter to a specified value. The parameter governing this behavior is autoupgrade allow-add-feature with a recommended setting of false. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.5 VMware Tools must limit the automatic addition of features

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Review VMware Tools configuration for automatic feature installation. Verify that automatic addition of optional Tools features is disabled or restricted unless explicitly required by the guest's management design.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, configure VMware Tools so optional features are not automatically added during reconfiguration/upgrade. Use the supported vmware- toolbox-cmd config set/Windows VMwareToolboxCmd.exe config set mechanism or enterprise deployment package and document required exceptions.

title: VMware Tools must limit the automatic removal of features
description: Limiting the automatic removal of features by VMware Tools during upgrade processes is crucial to maintain the intended security profile of the guest OS from vSphere. The automatic upgrade could potentially remove essential features, impacting the security posture inadvertently. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.6 VMware Tools must limit the automatic removal of features

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Review VMware Tools configuration for automatic feature removal. Verify that features are not automatically removed unless the behavior is explicitly approved.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, configure VMware Tools to prevent automatic removal of installed features during reconfiguration/upgrade unless required. Apply the guest-OS-specific VMware Tools configuration and validate application dependencies.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate GlobalConf unless required
description: The GlobalConf feature within VMware Tools facilitates the delivery of tools.conf configurations to virtual machines, simplifying configuration management. However, if not necessary, it's advisable to deactivate this feature to reduce potential security risks. The parameter governing this behavior is globalconf enabled with a recommended setting of false. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.7 VMware Tools must deactivate GlobalConf unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system 1. Execute `VMwareToolboxCmd.exe config get globalconf enabled```. Unless required, verify the value is false.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute VMwareToolboxCmd.exe equivalent. Restart VMware Tools if required and verify the setting.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate Guest Store Upgrade operations unless required
description: The GuestStore feature facilitates the distribution of specific content to multiple guests. If not required, it is advisable to disable this plugin to minimize potential attack vectors. The parameter governing this behavior is gueststoreupgrade policy with a recommended setting of off. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get gueststoreupgrade policy (or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe). Unless required, verify the value is off.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set gueststoreupgrade policy off or the Windows equivalent. Restart VMware Tools if required and verify the setting.
