This control is managed through a specific configuration parameter. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.12 VMware Tools must limit the use of MSI transforms when reconfiguring VMware Tools

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: On applicable Windows guests, execute VMwareToolboxCmd.exe config get autoupgrade allow-msi-transforms. Verify that the value is false. Treat this control as not applicable to non-Windows guests that do not use MSI.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute VMwareToolboxCmd.exe config set autoupgrade allow-msi-transforms false. Restart VMware Tools if required and verify the value remains false.

title: VMware Tools must enable VMware Tools logging
description: Enable logging within VMware Tools to ensure the collection of pertinent information, facilitating diagnostic or forensic activities. Logging within VMware Tools is highly customizable, allowing for tailored logging setups. The parameter governing this behavior is logging log with a recommended setting of true. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.13 VMware Tools must enable VMware Tools logging

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Review VMware Tools logging configuration inside the guest using vmware-toolbox-cmd config get logging log / the applicable tools.conf settings. Verify that Tools logging is enabled and produces expected log records.

remediation.command: Enable VMware Tools logging using the guest's supported tools.conf/vmware-toolbox- cmd config set mechanism. Restart the VMware Tools service if required and verify log generation.

title: VMware Tools must send VMware Tools logs to the system log service
description: Adjusting the logging destination in VMware Tools from the default file on disk to system log services streamlines log management. It redirects logs to syslog on Linux guests and the Windows Event Service on Microsoft Windows guests for centralized monitoring, management, and archiving. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.14 VMware Tools must send VMware Tools logs to the system log service

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Review VMware Tools logging destination and verify Tools messages are sent to the guest operating system's system logging facility (syslog/journald on Linux or the approved Windows logging mechanism) rather than only to an unmanaged local file.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, configure VMware Tools logging to use the system log service for the guest OS. Restart VMware Tools if required and verify a test Tools event reaches the system log.

title: Host integrated hardware management controller must secure authentication
description: Connections to centralized authentication sources, like Active Directory, should be disabled or carefully considered as attack vectors and dependency loops (for authentication, authorization, DNS, DHCP, and time). Consider managing local accounts on these devices through the APIs and CLI interfaces provided. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.8 Host integrated hardware management controller must secure authentication

audit.command: 1. Access the hardware management controller and verify that: ; Default credentials are not in use. ; Each administrator has an individually assigned account. ; Shared administrative accounts are avoided. ; Strong password requirements are enforced. ; Multi-factor authentication is enabled where supported. ; Directory- based authentication such as LDAP/AD is used where supported. ; Anonymous or unauthenticated access is disabled. ; Unused local accounts are disabled or removed. ; Account lockout / throttling is enabled. ; Management sessions time out after inactivity.

remediation.command: Recommended remediations by configuring authentication according to the approved security baseline: 1. Change all default passwords. 2. Disable or rename default accounts where the platform permits. 3. Create individually assigned administrator accounts. 4. Remove or disable unused accounts. 5. Enforce strong password complexity and minimum-length requirements. 6. Configure account lockout or login throttling after repeated authentication failures. 7. Enable MFA where supported. 8. Integrate the controller with approved centralized authentication such as Active Directory, LDAP, RADIUS, or TACACS+ where supported. 9.

title: Host hardware must enable AMD SEV-ES, if available
description: AMD EPYC platforms support SEV-ES, a technology to encrypt memory and CPU register state, and limit visibility to the hypervisor, in order to increase workload security and decrease exposure to certain types of attacks. When configured properly, vSphere supports the use of SEV-ES inside guest virtual machines and containers under vSphere and vSphere with Tanzu. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.9 Host hardware must enable AMD SEV-ES, if available

audit.command: 1. Execute: esxcfg-info | grep "\----\HV Support" or vsish -e cat /hardware/cpu/cpuInfo For an AMD host, the return value of 3 confirms AMD-V is enabled.

remediation.command: 1. Place the ESXi host into maintenance mode and reboot the physical server. 2. Enter the server BIOS/UEFI configuration and enable the AMD virtualization and memory-encryption features required by the platform.

title: Host hardware must enable Intel SGX, if available
description: Intel Xeon Scalable Processor platforms have Software Guard Extensions, or SGX, a technology that helps applications protect data in system memory. When configured properly, vSphere supports the use of SGX inside guest virtual machines. Enabling SGX in system firmware eases future enablement inside virtual machines and guest OSes. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.10 Host hardware must enable Intel SGX, if available

audit.command: 1. Identify processor vendor and model: esxcli hardware cpu list 2. Review the server BIOS/UEFI 3. Verify that SGX is enabled. Examples: Intel SGX = Enabled

remediation.command: 1. Place the ESXi host into maintenance mode 2. Reboot the physical server 3. Enter the server BIOS/UEFI configuration and enable Intel SGX.

title: Host hardware must secure unused external hardware ports
description: Unused ports, especially USB, can be used by attackers to attach storage, networking, and keyboards. Take reasonable steps to control access to these ports through disablement, access control, and/or with other means such as solid rack doors, rack side panels, and flooring that makes the ports inaccessible from outside the rack when the rack door is closed. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.11 Host hardware must secure unused external hardware ports

audit.command: Recommended physical interfaces to review and audit: USB ports SD-card slots Serial ports External PCIe expansion interfaces External management USB/vNIC interfaces Other removable-media or peripheral interfaces

remediation.command: 1. Place the ESXi host into maintenance mode if remediation will require a reboot. 2. Access the server BIOS/UEFI or hardware-management controller and disable unused external interfaces.

title: Host integrated hardware management controller must deactivate internal networking
description: Many servers have integrated hardware management controllers with the ability to present virtual network interfaces to ESXi as a management interface. These approaches create potential backdoors for access and are used by adversaries to circumvent network-based/perimeter firewalls, in either direction, and avoid observation by IDS/IPS/threat analysis tools. The audit runs esxcfg-advcfg -g /Net/BMCNetworkEnable and requires 0. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.12 Host integrated hardware management controller must deactivate internal networking

audit.command:
out=$(esxcfg-advcfg -g /Net/BMCNetworkEnable 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '{print $NF; exit}')
[ "$v" = 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "BMCNetworkEnable = $v"

remediation.guidance: To disable ESXi BMC internal networking: 1. execute esxcfg-advcfg -s 0 /Net/BMCNetworkEnable 2. execute esxcfg-advcfg -g /Net/BMCNetworkEnable Looking for: Value of BMCNetworkEnable is 0

title: Host must enable volatile key destruction
description: By default, ESXi ensures that pages allocated for virtual machines (VMs), userspace applications, and kernel threads are zeroed out at the time of allocation, to prevent the exposure of sensitive data like cryptographic keys to other clients. However, these keys can remain in host memory for an extended period if the memory is not reused. The audit reads Mem.MemEagerZero with esxcli and requires 1. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.12 Host must enable volatile key destruction

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Mem/MemEagerZero 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Mem/MemEagerZero: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Mem/MemEagerZero = $v (expected 1)"; fi

remediation.guidance: 1. Utilize the administrative PowerCLI session. 2. Execute: Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name Mem.MemEagerZero | Set-AdvancedSetting -Value 1 -Confirm:$false

title: Host should enable strict lockdown mode
description: Enabling lockdown mode disables direct local access to an ESXi host, requiring the host be managed remotely from vCenter Server. There are some operations, such as backup and troubleshooting, that require direct access to the host. In these cases, lockdown mode can be disabled on a temporary basis for specific hosts as needed, and then re-enabled when the task is completed. The audit runs vim-cmd -U dcui vimsvc/auth/lockdown_mode and requires lockdownStrict. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.21 Host should enable strict lockdown mode

audit.command:
out=$(vim-cmd -U dcui vimsvc/auth/lockdown_mode 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
case "$out" in *lockdownStrict*) echo compliant ;; *) echo "lockdown: $out" ;; esac

remediation.command: To enable lockdown mode, perform the following from the vSphere web client: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Select Configure then expand System and select Security Profile. 3. Across from Lockdown Mode click on Edit. 4. Click the radio button for Strict. 5. Click OK. Alternately, run the following PowerCLI command: # Enable lockdown mode for each host Get-VMHost | Foreach { $_.EnterLockdownMode() }

title: Host must deny shell access for the vpxuser account
description: Deactivating shell access for the vpxuser account enhances security by enforcing an "API only" stance for predefined non-root ESXi users such as vpxuser and dcui. The audit runs esxcli system account list and requires Shell Access false for vpxuser. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.23 Host must deny shell access for the vpxuser account

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system account list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="vpxuser" {print tolower($NF); exit}')
case "$v" in false) echo compliant ;; '') echo 'vpxuser not listed (or no Shell Access column on this build)'; exit 1 ;; *) echo 'vpxuser shell access: '"$v" ;; esac

remediation.command: Do not assign an interactive shell to vpxuser. If the account was altered, restore the vendor-supported no-shell configuration or reconnect/recreate the vCenter host management account using supported vCenter procedures.

title: Host should deactivate virtual hardware management network interfaces
description: Hardware management controllers may present virtual or USB NICs to the host, potentially serving as backdoors if left active. It's recommended to deactivate these interfaces both in the hardware configuration and within ESXi to prevent unauthorized access. The parameter governing this behavior is Net.BMCNetworkEnable with a recommended value of 0. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5 Host should deactivate virtual hardware management network interfaces

audit.command: Inspect host networking in the vSphere Client and with esxcli network ip interface list. Identify VMkernel interfaces used for hardware/BMC management or other virtual hardware management functions. Verify that such interfaces are absent unless explicitly required.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, remove or deactivate unnecessary virtual hardware management VMkernel interfaces and associated port groups. Keep out-of-band BMC/iDRAC/iLO management on dedicated physical management networks wherever possible.

title: Virtual machines must enable Secure Boot
description: Enable Secure Boot on virtual machines to ensure that only authenticated code runs from the firmware up through the operating system, thus providing a fundamental security measure against boot-time malware and unauthorized code execution. Expected: uefi.secureBoot.enabled = "TRUE". The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.1 Virtual machines must enable Secure Boot

audit.command:
command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk -v KEYRE='^uefi[.]secureboot[.]enabled$' -v MODE='eq' -v VAL='TRUE' 'BEGIN { re = tolower(KEYRE) }
{ line = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line); i = index(line, "="); if (i == 0) next
  k = tolower(substr(line, 1, i - 1)); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", k)
  v = substr(line, i + 1); sub(/^[ \t]*"?/, "", v); sub(/"?[ \t\r]*$/, "", v); v = tolower(v)
  if (k ~ re) { seen = 1; if (MODE == "not" && v == tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE != "not" && MODE != "ge" && v != tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE == "ge" && (v + 0) < (VAL + 0)) bad = bad " " k "=" v } }
END { if ((MODE == "eq" || MODE == "ge") && !seen) bad = " " KEYRE " not set"
      if (bad != "") print FILENAME ":" bad }' "$f"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.guidance: The following PowerCLI command may be used: $VMobj = (Get-VM -Name $VM) $ConfigSpec = New-Object VMware.Vim.VirtualMachineConfigSpec $bootOptions = New-Object VMware.Vim.VirtualMachineBootOptions $bootOptions.EfiSecureBootEnabled = $true $ConfigSpec.BootOptions = $bootOptions $task = $VMobj.ExtensionData.ReconfigVM_Task($ConfigSpec)

title: Virtual machines should deactivate 3D graphics features when not required
description: Due to performance reasons, modern graphic rendering is done within a dedicated graphic processing unit (GPU). Virtual machines can use the host-based GPU for such operations as well. Such dedicated hardware is typically accessed by using complex APIs like OpenGL and DirectX. This hardware-based 3D acceleration should be disabled if it is not needed. Expected: mks.enable3d absent or "FALSE". The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.4 Virtual machines should deactivate 3D graphics features when not required

audit.command:
command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk -v KEYRE='^mks[.]enable3d$' -v MODE='absent' -v VAL='FALSE' 'BEGIN { re = tolower(KEYRE) }
{ line = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line); i = index(line, "="); if (i == 0) next
  k = tolower(substr(line, 1, i - 1)); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", k)
  v = substr(line, i + 1); sub(/^[ \t]*"?/, "", v); sub(/"?[ \t\r]*$/, "", v); v = tolower(v)
  if (k ~ re) { seen = 1; if (MODE == "not" && v == tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE != "not" && MODE != "ge" && v != tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE == "ge" && (v + 0) < (VAL + 0)) bad = bad " " k "=" v } }
END { if ((MODE == "eq" || MODE == "ge") && !seen) bad = " " KEYRE " not set"
      if (bad != "") print FILENAME ":" bad }' "$f"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.guidance: The following PowerCLI command may be used: Get-VM -Name $VM | Get-AdvancedSetting mks.enable3d | Set-AdvancedSetting -Value FALSE

title: Virtual machines must remove unnecessary CD/DVD devices
description: Removing unnecessary devices from virtual machines minimizes the attack surface and reduces potential pathways for data exfiltration or unauthorized data capture. This practice aligns with the principle of least functionality, ensuring that VMs have only the essential components required to perform their designated functions. Expected: no ideX:Y/sataX:Y CD/DVD device with present = "TRUE". The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.15 Virtual machines must remove unnecessary CD/DVD devices

audit.command:
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk '{ line = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line); i = index(line, "="); if (i == 0) next
    k = tolower(substr(line, 1, i - 1)); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", k); v = substr(line, i + 1); sub(/^[ \t]*"?/, "", v); sub(/"?[ \t\r]*$/, "", v); v = tolower(v)
    if (k ~ /^(ide|sata)[0-9]+:[0-9]+\.devicetype$/ && v ~ /cdrom/) { p = k; sub(/\.devicetype$/, "", p); cd[p] = 1 }
    if (k ~ /^(ide|sata)[0-9]+:[0-9]+\.present$/) { p = k; sub(/\.present$/, "", p); pr[p] = v } }
    END { for (p in cd) if (pr[p] == "true") print FILENAME ": " p " CD/DVD present" }' "$f"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.command: To disconnect all CD/DVD drives from VMs, run the following PowerCLI command: # Remove all CD/DVD Drives attached to VMs Get-VM | Get-CDDrive | Remove-CDDrive The VM will need to be powered off for this change to take effect.

title: Virtual machines should have virtual machine hardware version 19 or newer
description: Upgrade to hardware version 19 or newer to access enhanced features and better performance. Test the upgrades and ensure compatibility across all operational landscapes. Expected: virtualHW.version 19 or newer. The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.29 Virtual machines should have virtual machine hardware version 19 or newer

audit.command:
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  v=$(sed -n 's/^ *virtualHW.version *= *"\{0,1\}\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$f" | head -n 1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 19 ] || echo "$f: virtualHW.version ${v:-unknown}"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.command: Before remediation, confirm guest OS and application compatibility, take required backups/snapshots according to policy, then use vSphere Client > Compatibility > Upgrade VM Compatibility or PowerCLI to upgrade to hardware version 19 or later. A VM power cycle may be required.

title: VMware Tools on deployed virtual machines must prevent being recustomized
description: Preventing re-customization of deployed virtual machines is essential to mitigate the risk of adversarial access through cloning and subsequent customization. Once a VM is deployed, it should be safeguarded against further customization to maintain the integrity of its configurations and data. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.4 VMware Tools on deployed virtual machines must prevent being recustomized

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Review VMware Tools guest customization settings on deployed VMs and verify deployed systems cannot be unexpectedly recustomized. Do not apply this control to templates where customization is intentionally required.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, disable post-deployment recustomization using the VMware Tools configuration supported for the guest OS and environment. Test provisioning/customization workflows first and retain customization capability only on approved templates or build images.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate ContainerInfo unless required
description: Deactivating the ContainerInfo plugin within VMware Tools is advised unless its functionality is required. This plugin collects data on running containers within a Linux guest operating system. The parameter governing this behavior is containerinfo poll- interval with a recommended setting of 0. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.8 VMware Tools must deactivate ContainerInfo unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get containerinfo poll-interval (or the Windows executable where applicable). Unless required, verify the polling interval is 0.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set containerinfo poll-interval 0 (or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe on Windows where supported). Restart Tools if required and verify the plugin no longer gathers container information.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate Appinfo information gathering unless required
description: Deactivating the Appinfo module, unless necessary, through VMware Tools is a prudent measure to minimize the attack surface. This module is designed for application discovery, but if not in use, it should be disabled. The parameter governing this behavior is appinfo disabled with a recommended setting of true. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.9 VMware Tools must deactivate Appinfo information gathering unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get appinfo disabled (or the Windows executable). Unless application discovery is required, verify the value is true.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set appinfo disabled true or the Windows equivalent. Restart Tools if required and verify AppInfo collection is disabled.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate Service Discovery unless required
description: The VMware Tools Service Discovery plugin is designed to connect to Aria Operations, furnishing it with additional data concerning guests and workloads. Disabling this plugin, when not in use, is a prudent step to diminish the attack surface. The parameter governing this behavior is servicediscovery disabled with a recommended setting of true. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.11 VMware Tools must deactivate Service Discovery unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get servicediscovery disabled (or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe). Unless Service Discovery is required, verify the value is true.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set servicediscovery disabled true or the Windows equivalent. Restart VMware Tools if required and verify the plugin is disabled.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate Guest Operations unless required
description: Guest Operations are a set of functions that underpin most host-to-guest interaction. Deactivating them reduces attack surface but also drastically reduces functionality. Ensure that your environment does not require these functions. Do not do this on template VMs. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 9.0 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.15 VMware Tools must deactivate Guest Operations unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get guestoperations disabled (or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe). Unless Guest Operations is required, verify the value is true. Do not treat templates requiring guest customization as automatically noncompliant without reviewing the operational need.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set guestoperations disabled true or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe config set guestoperations disabled true. Restart VMware Tools if required and test dependent workflows such as guest customization, backup, automation, and orchestration.

reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 1.10 Host hardware must enable Intel SGX, if available

description: Many servers have integrated hardware management controllers with the ability to present virtual network interfaces to ESXi as a management interface. These approaches create potential backdoors for access and are used by adversaries to circumvent network-based/perimeter firewalls, in either direction, and avoid observation by IDS/IPS/threat analysis tools. The audit runs esxcfg-advcfg -g /Net/BMCNetworkEnable and requires 0. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 1.12 Host integrated hardware management controller must deactivate internal networking

audit.command:
out=$(esxcfg-advcfg -g /Net/BMCNetworkEnable 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '{print $NF; exit}')
[ "$v" = 0 ] && echo compliant || echo "BMCNetworkEnable = $v"

remediation.guidance: To disable ESXi BMC internal networking: 1. execute esxcfg-advcfg -s 0 /Net/BMCNetworkEnable 2. execute esxcfg-advcfg -g /Net/BMCNetworkEnable Looking for: Value of BMCNetworkEnable is 0

title: Host must enable volatile key destruction
description: By default, ESXi ensures that pages allocated for virtual machines (VMs), userspace applications, and kernel threads are zeroed out at the time of allocation, to prevent the exposure of sensitive data like cryptographic keys to other clients. However, these keys can remain in host memory for an extended period if the memory is not reused. The audit reads Mem.MemEagerZero with esxcli and requires 1. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 2.12 Host must enable volatile key destruction

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system settings advanced list -o /Mem/MemEagerZero 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="Int" && $2=="Value:" {print $3; exit}')
case "$v" in ''|*[!0-9-]*) echo '/Mem/MemEagerZero: no integer value'; exit 1 ;; esac
if [ "$v" -eq 1 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "/Mem/MemEagerZero = $v (expected 1)"; fi

remediation.guidance: 1. Utilize the administrative PowerCLI session. 2. Execute: Get-VMHost | Get-AdvancedSetting -Name Mem.MemEagerZero | Set- AdvancedSetting -Value 1 -Confirm:$false

title: Host should enable strict lockdown mode
description: Enabling lockdown mode disables direct local access to an ESXi host, requiring the host be managed remotely from vCenter Server. There are some operations, such as backup and troubleshooting, that require direct access to the host. In these cases, lockdown mode can be disabled on a temporary basis for specific hosts as needed, and then re-enabled when the task is completed. The audit runs vim-cmd -U dcui vimsvc/auth/lockdown_mode and requires lockdownStrict. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 3.21 Host should enable strict lockdown mode

audit.command:
out=$(vim-cmd -U dcui vimsvc/auth/lockdown_mode 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
case "$out" in *lockdownStrict*) echo compliant ;; *) echo "lockdown: $out" ;; esac

remediation.command: To enable lockdown mode, perform the following from the vSphere web client: 1. From the vSphere Web Client, select the host. 2. Select Configure then expand System and select Security Profile. 3. Across from Lockdown Mode click on Edit. 4. Click the radio button for Strict. 5. Click OK. Alternately, run the following PowerCLI command: # Enable lockdown mode for each host Get-VMHost | Foreach { $_.EnterLockdownMode() }

title: Host must deny shell access for the vpxuser account
description: Deactivating shell access for the vpxuser account enhances security by enforcing an "API only" stance for predefined non-root ESXi users such as vpxuser and dcui. The audit runs esxcli system account list and requires Shell Access false for vpxuser. Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 3.23 Host must deny shell access for the vpxuser account

audit.command:
out=$(esxcli system account list 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
v=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1=="vpxuser" {print tolower($NF); exit}')
case "$v" in false) echo compliant ;; '') echo 'vpxuser not listed (or no Shell Access column on this build)'; exit 1 ;; *) echo 'vpxuser shell access: '"$v" ;; esac

remediation.command: Do not assign an interactive shell to vpxuser. If the account was altered, restore the vendor-supported no-shell configuration or reconnect/recreate the vCenter host management account using supported vCenter procedures.

title: Host should deactivate virtual hardware management network interfaces
description: Hardware management controllers may present virtual or USB NICs to the host, potentially serving as backdoors if left active. It's recommended to deactivate these interfaces both in the hardware configuration and within ESXi to prevent unauthorized access. The parameter governing this behavior is Net.BMCNetworkEnable with a recommended value of 0. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 5.5 Host should deactivate virtual hardware management network interfaces

audit.command: Inspect host networking in the vSphere Client and with esxcli network ip interface list. Identify VMkernel interfaces used for hardware/BMC management or other virtual hardware management functions. Verify that such interfaces are absent unless explicitly required.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, remove or deactivate unnecessary virtual hardware management VMkernel interfaces and associated port groups. Keep out-of-band BMC/iDRAC/iLO management on dedicated physical management networks wherever possible.

title: Virtual machines must enable Secure Boot
description: Enable Secure Boot on virtual machines to ensure that only authenticated code runs from the firmware up through the operating system, thus providing a fundamental security measure against boot-time malware and unauthorized code execution. Expected: uefi.secureBoot.enabled = "TRUE". The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 7.1 Virtual machines must enable Secure Boot

audit.command:
command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk -v KEYRE='^uefi[.]secureboot[.]enabled$' -v MODE='eq' -v VAL='TRUE' 'BEGIN { re = tolower(KEYRE) }
{ line = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line); i = index(line, "="); if (i == 0) next
  k = tolower(substr(line, 1, i - 1)); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", k)
  v = substr(line, i + 1); sub(/^[ \t]*"?/, "", v); sub(/"?[ \t\r]*$/, "", v); v = tolower(v)
  if (k ~ re) { seen = 1; if (MODE == "not" && v == tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE != "not" && MODE != "ge" && v != tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE == "ge" && (v + 0) < (VAL + 0)) bad = bad " " k "=" v } }
END { if ((MODE == "eq" || MODE == "ge") && !seen) bad = " " KEYRE " not set"
      if (bad != "") print FILENAME ":" bad }' "$f"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.guidance: The following PowerCLI command may be used: $VMobj = (Get-VM -Name $VM) $ConfigSpec = New-Object VMware.Vim.VirtualMachineConfigSpec $bootOptions = New-Object VMware.Vim.VirtualMachineBootOptions $bootOptions.EfiSecureBootEnabled = $true $ConfigSpec.BootOptions = $bootOptions $task = $VMobj.ExtensionData.ReconfigVM_Task($ConfigSpec)

title: Virtual machines should deactivate 3D graphics features when not required
description: Due to performance reasons, modern graphic rendering is done within a dedicated graphic processing unit (GPU). Virtual machines can use the host-based GPU for such operations as well. Such dedicated hardware is typically accessed by using complex APIs like OpenGL and DirectX. This hardware-based 3D acceleration should be disabled if it is not needed. Expected: mks.enable3d absent or "FALSE". The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 7.4 Virtual machines should deactivate 3D graphics features when not required

audit.command:
command -v find >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk -v KEYRE='^mks[.]enable3d$' -v MODE='absent' -v VAL='FALSE' 'BEGIN { re = tolower(KEYRE) }
{ line = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line); i = index(line, "="); if (i == 0) next
  k = tolower(substr(line, 1, i - 1)); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", k)
  v = substr(line, i + 1); sub(/^[ \t]*"?/, "", v); sub(/"?[ \t\r]*$/, "", v); v = tolower(v)
  if (k ~ re) { seen = 1; if (MODE == "not" && v == tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE != "not" && MODE != "ge" && v != tolower(VAL)) bad = bad " " k "=" v
                else if (MODE == "ge" && (v + 0) < (VAL + 0)) bad = bad " " k "=" v } }
END { if ((MODE == "eq" || MODE == "ge") && !seen) bad = " " KEYRE " not set"
      if (bad != "") print FILENAME ":" bad }' "$f"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.guidance: The following PowerCLI command may be used: Get-VM -Name $VM | Get-AdvancedSetting mks.enable3d | Set-AdvancedSetting - Value FALSE

title: Virtual machines must remove unnecessary CD/DVD devices
description: Removing unnecessary devices from virtual machines minimizes the attack surface and reduces potential pathways for data exfiltration or unauthorized data capture. This practice aligns with the principle of least functionality, ensuring that VMs have only the essential components required to perform their designated functions. Expected: no ideX:Y/sataX:Y CD/DVD device with present = "TRUE". The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 7.15 Virtual machines must remove unnecessary CD/DVD devices

audit.command:
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  awk '{ line = $0; sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line); i = index(line, "="); if (i == 0) next
    k = tolower(substr(line, 1, i - 1)); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", k); v = substr(line, i + 1); sub(/^[ \t]*"?/, "", v); sub(/"?[ \t\r]*$/, "", v); v = tolower(v)
    if (k ~ /^(ide|sata)[0-9]+:[0-9]+\.devicetype$/ && v ~ /cdrom/) { p = k; sub(/\.devicetype$/, "", p); cd[p] = 1 }
    if (k ~ /^(ide|sata)[0-9]+:[0-9]+\.present$/) { p = k; sub(/\.present$/, "", p); pr[p] = v } }
    END { for (p in cd) if (pr[p] == "true") print FILENAME ": " p " CD/DVD present" }' "$f"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.command: To disconnect all CD/DVD drives from VMs, run the following PowerCLI command: # Remove all CD/DVD Drives attached to VMs Get-VM | Get-CDDrive | Remove-CDDrive The VM will need to be powered off for this change to take effect.

title: Virtual machines should have virtual machine hardware version 19 or newer
description: Upgrade to hardware version 19 or newer to access enhanced features and better performance. Test the upgrades and ensure compatibility across all operational landscapes. Expected: virtualHW.version 19 or newer. The audit parses every .vmx file under /vmfs/volumes/ on the host and lists the VMs that do not comply; it passes when none are found (or no VMs exist). Runs in the ESXi Shell (busybox sh) as root.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 7.29 Virtual machines should have virtual machine hardware version 19 or newer

audit.command:
out=$(find /vmfs/volumes/ -maxdepth 3 -type f -name '*.vmx' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do
  v=$(sed -n 's/^ *virtualHW.version *= *"\{0,1\}\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$f" | head -n 1)
  [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 19 ] || echo "$f: virtualHW.version ${v:-unknown}"
done)
[ -z "$out" ] && echo compliant || printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -n 25

remediation.command: Before remediation, confirm guest OS and application compatibility, take required backups/snapshots according to policy, then use vSphere Client > Compatibility > Upgrade VM Compatibility or PowerCLI to upgrade to hardware version 19 or later. A VM power cycle may be required.

title: VMware Tools on deployed virtual machines must prevent being recustomized
description: Preventing re-customization of deployed virtual machines is essential to mitigate the risk of adversarial access through cloning and subsequent customization. Once a VM is deployed, it should be safeguarded against further customization to maintain the integrity of its configurations and data. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.4 VMware Tools on deployed virtual machines must prevent being recustomized

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Review VMware Tools guest customization settings on deployed VMs and verify deployed systems cannot be unexpectedly recustomized. Do not apply this control to templates where customization is intentionally required.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, disable post-deployment recustomization using the VMware Tools configuration supported for the guest OS and environment. Test provisioning/customization workflows first and retain customization capability only on approved templates or build images.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate ContainerInfo unless required
description: Deactivating the ContainerInfo plugin within VMware Tools is advised unless its functionality is required. This plugin collects data on running containers within a Linux guest operating system. The parameter governing this behavior is containerinfo poll- interval with a recommended setting of 0. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.8 VMware Tools must deactivate ContainerInfo unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get containerinfo poll-interval (or the Windows executable where applicable). Unless required, verify the polling interval is 0.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set containerinfo poll-interval 0 (or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe on Windows where supported). Restart Tools if required and verify the plugin no longer gathers container information.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate Appinfo information gathering unless required
description: Deactivating the Appinfo module, unless necessary, through VMware Tools is a prudent measure to minimize the attack surface. This module is designed for application discovery, but if not in use, it should be disabled. The parameter governing this behavior is appinfo disabled with a recommended setting of true. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.9 VMware Tools must deactivate Appinfo information gathering unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get appinfo disabled (or the Windows executable). Unless application discovery is required, verify the value is true.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set appinfo disabled true or the Windows equivalent. Restart Tools if required and verify AppInfo collection is disabled.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate Service Discovery unless required
description: The VMware Tools Service Discovery plugin is designed to connect to Aria Operations, furnishing it with additional data concerning guests and workloads. Disabling this plugin, when not in use, is a prudent step to diminish the attack surface. The parameter governing this behavior is servicediscovery disabled with a recommended setting of true. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.11 VMware Tools must deactivate Service Discovery unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get servicediscovery disabled (or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe). Unless Service Discovery is required, verify the value is true.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set servicediscovery disabled true or the Windows equivalent. Restart VMware Tools if required and verify the plugin is disabled.

title: VMware Tools must deactivate Guest Operations unless required
description: Guest Operations are a set of functions that underpin most host-to-guest interaction. Deactivating them reduces attack surface but also drastically reduces functionality. Ensure that your environment does not require these functions. Do not do this on template VMs. Manual review: the check needs vCenter/PowerCLI, firmware or guest access, or an organization-specific value.
reference: CIS VMware ESXi 8.0 Benchmark v1.4.0 - 8.15 VMware Tools must deactivate Guest Operations unless required

audit.command: Inside each guest OS: Within the guest operating system, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config get guestoperations disabled (or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe). Unless Guest Operations is required, verify the value is true. Do not treat templates requiring guest customization as automatically noncompliant without reviewing the operational need.

remediation.command: To remediate this recommendation, execute vmware-toolbox-cmd config set guestoperations disabled true or VMwareToolboxCmd.exe config set guestoperations disabled true. Restart VMware Tools if required and test dependent workflows such as guest customization, backup, automation, and orchestration.
